slides.say: A E is a diameter of a circle with center O. B, C and D lie on the same semicircle, in that order. Given: A B, B C, C D and D E are all equal, and A O is five centimeters. Which of the following statements is not true?
We're looking for the one statement that is surely not true. [short pause] So we go statement by statement. A statement that's always true, or even possible, is out, and we hope to be left with one.
at: So we go statement by statement

slides.say: Statement one. Angle D A E equals angle C A D. Lots of letters, so let's go slowly. D A E is the angle at A between A E and A D. Let's call it alpha.
C A D is the angle at A between A D and A C. Let's call it beta.

Both are inscribed angles. Alpha intercepts the arc D E, and beta intercepts the arc C D. The chords D E and C D are equal, so their arcs are equal too. And inscribed angles on equal arcs are equal. So alpha equals beta.
Statement one is surely true, so choice number one is out.
at: so choice number one is out

slides.say: [pause] Statement two. Angle B O C is forty-five degrees. Let's call it x. Its vertex is at the center, so it's a central angle. To see it, let's draw the radii from O to B, to C and to D.
Equal chords give equal central angles. All four chords are equal, so all four central angles are x.
at: so all four central angles are x

slides.say: Together, the four angles make the straight angle A O E, one hundred eighty degrees. So four x is one hundred eighty. To divide by four, you can halve twice. Half of one hundred eighty is ninety, and half of ninety is forty-five. So x really is forty-five, and choice number two is out.
at: and choice number two is out

slides.say: [pause] Statement three. Angle A D E is ninety degrees. That's the angle at D, between D A and D E.
at: Angle A D E is ninety

slides.say: It's an inscribed angle that lies on the diameter A E. An inscribed angle on a diameter is always ninety, because it's half of the central angle, and the central angle on a diameter is a straight angle, one hundred eighty. So it's true, and choice number three is out.
at: An inscribed angle on a diameter
and choice number three is out

slides.say: On the exam, we're done. Three statements are out, so you mark choice number four and move on. There's no time to check it.
at: so you mark choice number four

slides.say: [pause] But we're in a lesson, so let's check it. Is A C five root three? Look at triangle A O C. We need O C, so let's draw it, from O to C.
A O is a radius, five. O C is a radius too, so it's also five. And angle A O C is made of two of our equal central angles, so it's forty-five plus forty-five, which is ninety.
So triangle A O C is a right triangle with two equal legs. That's the silver triangle, forty-five, forty-five, ninety. In the silver triangle, the hypotenuse is the leg times root two.

So A C is five root two, not five root three. Root three belongs to the gold triangle. So statement four is the one that's not true. Choice number four is our answer. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: So A C is five root two
Choice number four is our answer
